newsitem.title: JAPAN: Kansai Electric to ask US firms to process uranium.
newsitem.headline: Kansai Electric to ask US firms to process uranium.

text.p: Kansai Electric Power Co Inc said on Monday it plans to place an order with U.S. firms Westinghouse Electric Corp and Siemens Power Corp to process uranium fuel in a bid to cut costs.
Siemens Power is the U.S. subsidiary of German electronics group Siemens AG.

Kansai Electric is planning to place an order with the two U.S. firms to carry out the reconversion and fabrication of about 10 percent of its annual nuclear fuel requirements, a company spokesman said.
Reconversion is a chemical process in which enriched gaseous uranium is turned into powdered uranium dioxide.
The fabrication process transforms the powdered uranium dioxide into cylindrical pellets to be used in nuclear power plants.
In the past, two Japanese firms -- Mitsubishi Nuclear Fuel Co Ltd and Nuclear Fuel Industries Ltd -- have carried out reconversion and fabrication for the power firm.
It is not yet clear how much the new arrangement could save Kansai Electric as the company has not reached a final agreement with the U.S. firms, the spokesman said.
The utility firm buys about 200 tonnes of processed uranium fuel, which costs 17 billion yen, he said.

Regional power firms in Japan, including Kansai Electric, announced earlier this month that they plan to cut electricity prices next year amid mounting pressure to bring Japan's electricity rates into line with international levels.
The Japanese government, however, is urging the power firms to cut their rates again in 2000.

Electricity for industrial purposes costs about 25 percent more in Japan than in Germany and 30 percent more than in the United States, according to an estimate by the Ministry of International Trade and Industry.
